feature: Third-party extension lifecycle improvements and TYTY compatibility diagnosis
changes: Allow an installed extension to be disabled while it is loading; continue blocking changes during an installation transaction.
Skip stale queued enable operations and hide extension actions while disabled or loading.
Wrap native extension popups with a system Done control; prevent duplicate popups and dismiss only the owning extension popup when unloading.
Normalize explicit wildcard ports in externally_connectable matches in the private prepared manifest. Preserve fixed ports, hosts, paths, permissions and the original source package.

unit.status: 8 passed, 0 failures, 0 skipped on iOS 26.2 simulator
coverage: Cancel repeated queued enable operations, retain disabled state and re-enable successfully
Popup close control exists; disabling another owner does not dismiss it; disabling its owner does
Failed enable restores disabled state and a diagnostic
Script updates retain stored values and disabled state; deletion removes script access
Wildcard-port normalization is idempotent and leaves numeric ports, source and permissions unchanged
A real native extension background receives and replies to an external localhost message on an ephemeral port
Existing background wrapper migration stays idempotent
Undeclared native compatibility permissions remain rejected

validation.popup_visual_review: Reviewed exported third-party-extension-popup-close screenshot: extension content, title and system Done control visible.
validation.localization: check_localization.py --strict passed: 881 keys, 489 ReadingTools keys and 81 FeatureImprovements keys across 50 locales
validation.metadata: export_metadata_json.py --check passed; version and metadata unchanged
validation.earlier_harness_failures: Retained in artifacts. Fixed missing fixture destination directory and used a structured JavaScript reply/error envelope instead of a bare asynchronous result. Final assertions still require the actual native message reply.

tyty.installation: The package extracts, previews and loads into a native WKWebExtensionContext. Installation alone is not functional certification.

confirmed_findings.issue: Website expects a fixed Chrome extension ID
confirmed_findings.evidence: The live website messaging code passes kmibgmblaakbhikfbjaincmnmabgnoim to chrome.runtime.sendMessage; this matches the CRX3 identity. Soulo assigns record.id.uuidString as context.uniqueIdentifier and has no Chrome-ID alias routing.
confirmed_findings.impact: The website detection request targets a different ID, so it cannot reach this installed context.
confirmed_findings.status: Dedicated compatibility work still required; native storage identity was not changed.

confirmed_findings.evidence: A minimal document-background control returned pong after port normalization; the production normalizer also passes an independent native round-trip regression.
confirmed_findings.status: Fixed generically in private prepared manifests. This alone does not fix the website ID or background business code.

additional_diagnostic_observations: Instrumented service-worker probes did not complete the startup callback within 8 seconds and returned no ping reply, including a minimal worker control. This does not establish that TYTY business code alone causes the startup failure.
Document-background adaptations of the original source hit a runtime syntax error even though static JSContext parsing passed. These adaptations were diagnostic only and are not shipped.

A diagnostic template-literal-transformed document background progressed to a native declarativeNetRequest error: rule ID 2 regexFilter was rejected as unsupported. Its synchronous startup call then prevents listener registration. This observation belongs to the adapted probe, not a functional certification of the stock worker.
The template transform, background replacement, logging instrumentation and rule stubs were not included in production.
tyty.status: Resolved for the pinned 0.6.6 package in 1.2.14; real-package messaging, request forwarding, rules and lifecycle verification passed. See superseding report for scope and limits.
tyty.business_limits: No account login, cloud file transfer, upload or deletion was attempted. No evidence established a conflict with built-in user scripts.
tyty.initial_status: Not fully supported or certified. A website ID bridge and validated background/network-rule adaptation remain necessary.

limits: Native extension tests require iOS 18.4 or later.
snapshot_stage: Initial diagnosis before the 1.2.14 follow-up; diagnostic observations below are historical.
